BIOL 111.title: Introduction to Modern Biology
BIOL 111.description: Concepts fundamental to biological issues, such as the genetic basis of biological variation, evolution, infectious diseases, causes of cancer, population growth, and human effects on ecosystems. Not open to students who have credit for Biology 12 (including AP, IB).

BIOL 112.title: Biology of the Cell
BIOL 112.description: The principles of cellular and molecular biology using bacterial and eukaryotic examples.
BIOL 112.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 12, CHEM 100, CHEM 110, CHEM 111 and one of BIOL 11, BIOL 12, BIOL 111

BIOL 121.title: Genetics, Evolution and Ecology
BIOL 121.description: Principles of storage and transmission of genetic variation; origin and evolution of species and their ecological interactions.

BIOL 140.title: Laboratory Investigations in Life Science
BIOL 140.description: Guided experimental investigations of biological questions.

BIOL 153.title: Human Biology: Anatomy and Physiology
BIOL 153.description: The principles of biology with particular reference to the human body (anatomy and physiology). Laboratories include selected experiments on organ physiology and general anatomy. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: .
BIOL 153.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 12, CHEM_V 100, CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111 and one of BIOL 11, BIOL_V 12, BIOL_V 111

BIOL 155.title: Human Biology: Physiology and Introductory Anatomy
BIOL 155.description: The principles of biology with particular reference to the human body (anatomy and physiology). (physiology and introductory anatomy). Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 155.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 12, CHEM 100, CHEM 110, CHEM 111 and one of BIOL 11, BIOL 12, BIOL 111

BIOL 180.title: Thinking Like a Life Scientist
BIOL 180.description: Science as a process, the skills of scientists, and the exploration of a current biological challenge with a practicing UBC scientist.

BIOL 200.title: Fundamentals of Cell Biology
BIOL 200.description: Structure and function of plant and animal cells; membrane models, cytoplasmic organelles, biological information from gene to protein, the endomembrane system, secretion, intracellular digestion, endocytosis, transport processes, cytoskeleton and cell motility.

children.raw: 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL_V and 6 credits of first-year CHEM_V

BIOL 200.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL_V 112 and one of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130 or (b) SCIE_V 001 or (c) 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL_V and 6 credits of first-year CHEM_V or (d) one of BIOL_V 112 or BIOL_V 121 and a corequisite of one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_O 203

BIOL 201.title: Introduction to Biochemistry
BIOL 201.description: Biological molecules, protein structure and enzyme action, energy transfer, central metabolic pathways and their regulation. Examples drawn from plants, animals and microorganisms. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)
BIOL 201.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 200 or BIOL_O 200 and one of CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 260, CHEM_O 213; or BIOL_V 200 or BIOL_O 200 and a corequisite of CHEM_V 213 or CHEM_O 204; or a corequisite of either CHEM_V 313 or CHEM_V 330

BIOL 203.title: Eukaryotic Microbiology
BIOL 203.description: Introduction to the origin and diversity of protists (protozoa and algae) at both cellular and genomic levels, including the role of endosymbiosis in evolution.
BIOL 203.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. Or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 204.title: Vertebrate Structure and Function
BIOL 204.description: Introduction to the vertebrate phyla and their evolution; a comparative study of vertebrate structure and function, with dissection of representative forms.
BIOL 204.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. Or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 205.title: Comparative Invertebrate Zoology
BIOL 205.description: An introduction to the unity, diversity and evolutionary history of invertebrates.
BIOL 205.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. Or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 209.title: Biodiversity of Algae, Fungi and Bryophytes
BIOL 209.description: Diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolutionary origins of multicellular eukaryotes, illustrated through mosses and liverworts; fungi and slime molds; and fresh water and marine algae.
BIOL 209.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. Or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 210.title: Vascular Plants
BIOL 210.description: A comparative study of pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, integrating form, function and ecology.
BIOL 210.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001. or 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 230.title: Fundamentals of Ecology
BIOL 230.description: Dynamics of plant and animal populations, structure of ecological communities and functioning of ecosystems. Interpretation of research results and application to environmental issues. Labs meet once a month. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 230.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, SCIE 001 or 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL

BIOL 233.title: Genetics for Life
BIOL 233.description: How genetic differences determine individual characteristics, and how they are inherited, analyzed, and modified. Emphasis on genetic diversity, human ancestry, personal genomics, and cancer genetics.
BIOL 233.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOL 112, BIOL 121 or (b) SCIE 001. ; or (c) a corequisite of one of CHEM 203 or CHEM 223 and one of BIOL 112 or BIOL 121

BIOL 234.title: Fundamentals of Genetics
BIOL 234.description: Genotype and phenotype, mechanisms of inheritance, genetic analysis. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 234.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 121 or (b) SCIE_V 001 or (c) a corequisite of one of CHEM_V 203 or CHEM_V 223 or CHEM_O 203 and one of BIOL_V 112 or BIOL_V 121 or (d) 8 transfer credits of first-year BIOL_V

BIOL 260.title: Fundamentals of Physiology
BIOL 260.description: Principles of cellular and organismal physiology illustrated with examples from unicellular organisms, plants and animals, focusing on transport processes, water balance, nutrient acquisition and communication.

children.raw: 8 transfer credits of 1st year BIOL and 6 credits of 1st year chemistry

BIOL 260.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOL 112, BIOL 121 or (b) SCIE 001. or (c) 8 transfer credits of 1st year BIOL and 6 credits of 1st year chemistry

BIOL 300.title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
BIOL 300.description: Statistical procedures for biological research; estimation, hypothesis testing, goodness of fit, analysis of variance and regression; use of computers for statistical analysis. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 300.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 180, SCIE_V 001

BIOL 301.title: Biomathematics
BIOL 301.description: Introduction to uses of mathematics in the biological sciences; experimental design and modelling of biological processes. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: Recommended co-requisites: one of BIOL 300, STAT 200.

BIOL 302.title: Biodiversity, Human & Planetary Health
BIOL 302.description: Effects of biodiversity on human health, from human microbiome to ecosystem. Strategies for protecting, restoring and managing for biodiversity, human and planetary health.
BIOL 302.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 111, BIOL 121, GEOS 207, SCIE 001 and third-year class standing

BIOL 303.title: Green Planet: Biology and History of Plants that Changed Civilizations
BIOL 303.description: Biological, cultural, and societal significance of staple crops selected as foods, medicines or raw materials by different societies, and their pivotal role in the rise and fall of past and present civilizations.

BIOL 306.title: Advanced Ecology
BIOL 306.description: Ecology of populations, communities and ecosystems. Tests of ecological theory with experiments and application to environmental issues. Labs meet once a month. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

BIOL 307.title: Natural History Collections and Biodiversity Science
BIOL 307.description: An introduction to biodiversity and specimen-based science, including theory and best practices for creating, curating and preserving natural history collections, working ethically with collections, and the historical, contemporary and future role of these collections to science and society. Pre-requisites: A minimum of 3rd-year class standing or higher.

BIOL 310.title: Introduction to Animal Behaviour
BIOL 310.description: Animal behavior from an ecological and evolutionary perspective; the methods used to study behaviour and test its adaptive significance.
BIOL 310.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001; and 3rd-year class standing or higher

BIOL 311.title: Experimental Methods in Animal Behaviour
BIOL 311.description: Designing, conducting, and analyzing studies of animal behaviour, with an emphasis on field-based methods. Students conduct capstone research projects. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

BIOL 314.title: Elements of Biodiversity
BIOL 314.description: The units of biodiversity, from genes to ecosystems, how they are structured in space, and their importance to human well-being and ecosystem health.
BIOL 314.prerequisiteText: One of APBI 260, BIOL 230, FRST 201, GEOB 207, GEOS 207

BIOL 317.title: Weed Science
BIOL 317.description: Importance, identification, dissemination and biology of weeds; preventative, cultural, biological and chemical methods of control.

BIOL 320.title: Survey of Algae
BIOL 320.description: A survey of the algae, considering their morphology, life history, classification, and ecology.

BIOL 321.title: Morphology and Evolution of Bryophytes
BIOL 321.description: A study of evolution, taxonomy and morphology of mosses, liverworts and hornworts with emphasis on living plants in their environment.

BIOL 322.title: Structure and Evolution of Ferns and Fern-allies
BIOL 322.description: Anatomy, morphology and relationships of the ferns and fern-allies, with assessment of both fossil and extant taxa.

BIOL 323.title: Structure and Reproduction of Fungi
BIOL 323.description: The evolutionary diversity of the fungi as shown by their morphology and reproductive biology.

BIOL 324.title: Introduction to Seed Plant Taxonomy
BIOL 324.description: Introduction to seed plant taxonomy emphasizing descriptive morphology and identification. Each student will be required to submit a plant collection.

BIOL 325.title: Introduction to Animal Mechanics and Locomotion
BIOL 325.description: Comparative aspects of the functional design of skeletal systems and the mechanics of swimming, flying and terrestrial locomotion, with particular reference to the vertebrates.

BIOL 326.title: Experimental Biology of Invertebrates
BIOL 326.description: Behaviour and ecology of invertebrates as revealed by hands-on experiments in the laboratory and field. Marine emphasis.

BIOL 327.title: Introduction to Entomology
BIOL 327.description: A survey of the structure, classification and biology of insects; ecology, life-histories and insect-plant relations.

BIOL 328.title: Ecology and Evolution of Parasites
BIOL 328.description: Morphology, life histories, ecology and evolution of parasites (and infectious agents more broadly) infecting humans and animals.

BIOL 329.title: Cell Receptor Signaling, Communication and Regulation
BIOL 329.description: How cells react to external signals, and how these responses are regulated. Experimental approaches and common themes will be examined using a variety of cell receptors as models. .

BIOL 330.title: Developmental Biology (Lecture)
BIOL 330.description: Animal development and its underlying causal principles; introductory embryology.
BIOL 330.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL 201 or (b) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234

BIOL 331.title: Developmental Biology
BIOL 331.description: Animal development and its underlying causal principles; introductory embryology.
BIOL 331.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL 201 or (b) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234

BIOL 332.title: Protistology
BIOL 332.description: Cell biology, ecology, and evolution of protists; origins of multicellularity; the role of protists in micropaleontology, parasitology, and oceanography.

BIOL 335.title: Molecular Genetics
BIOL 335.description: Isolation and identification of genes, analysis of gene structure; gene expression and its regulation in prokaryotes and in eukaryotes; developmental genetics.
BIOL 335.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 233, BIOL 234, MICB 322, FRST 302

BIOL 336.title: Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology
BIOL 336.description: Natural selection; population genetics, quantitative genetics and systematics; classical and molecular approaches to the study of evolution.

BIOL 337.title: Introductory Genetics Laboratory
BIOL 337.description: A laboratory course demonstrating the fundamental principles of inheritance: Mendel's Laws, sex-linkage, mapping, mutagenesis, chromosome structure, developmental biology, biochemical and population genetics.

BIOL 338.title: Introduction to Genomics
BIOL 338.description: An introduction to genome biology and applications of genomics.

BIOL 340.title: Introductory Cell Biology Laboratory
BIOL 340.description: Designing and conducting cell biology experiments using unicellular eukaryotes or prokaryotes with emphasis on techniques in microscopy and cell biology.

children.raw: 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science
3rd-year class standing in Combined Honours Biophysics

BIOL 340.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 200 and 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science and one of (a) BIOL_V 180 (or BIOL_V 140), or (b) SCIE_V 001, or (c) 3rd-year class standing in Combined Honours Biophysics

BIOL 341.title: Introductory Molecular Biology Laboratory
BIOL 341.description: Designing and conducting molecular biology experiments using bioinformatics recombinant DNA techniques.

children.raw: 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science

BIOL 341.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 200 and 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science

BIOL 342.title: Integrative Biology Laboratory
BIOL 342.description: Field-based and laboratory-based investigation of organisms.

children.raw: Third-year standing or higher in Combined Major in Science,

BIOL 342.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing or higher in Combined Major in Science, and one of (a) BIOL 121 and BIOL 180 (or BIOL 140), or (b) SCIE 001, or (c) 8 transfer credits of first-year biology

BIOL 343.title: Plants and Peoples
BIOL 343.description: The interactions of plants and human societies: the role of people in the origin, evolution and dispersal of food, drug and economic plants, and the influences of plants on human societies. Suitable for upper-level Arts students.

BIOL 344.title: Human Heredity and Evolution
BIOL 344.description: Relates genetic and evolutionary concepts to humans. Primarily for upper-level students in the Faculty of Arts. Not open to students in the Life Sciences.

BIOL 345.title: Human Ecology
BIOL 345.description: Basics of ecology are introduced, focussing on observations of the natural world. Assignments, including a group project, consider connections between research, awareness and practical uses of ecology. Not for credit in the Life Sciences.

BIOL 346.title: Microbes and Society
BIOL 346.description: An elementary course in molecular biology primarily for Arts students. The historical development of recent discoveries in molecular biology with emphasis on bacteria and viruses and their interaction with humans. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.) Not for credit in Life Sciences.

BIOL 347.title: Principles and Methodology in Biological Research
BIOL 347.description: Contemporary research in the Botany and Zoology Departments; history and methodology of scientific discovery; seminars on current problems. Restricted to Honours students in Biology. Not to be taken concurrently with BIOL 449.

BIOL 348.title: Biology of Cannabis
BIOL 348.description: Biological aspects of cannabis, including structure and function, photosynthesis, plant growth, specialized metabolites, neuroscience and the human endocannabinoid system, and applications for human use in medicine, consumer products and textiles.

BIOL 350.title: Darwinian Medicine
BIOL 350.description: Using the Darwinian theory of natural selection to explore explanations of infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, mental illness, and other human diseases. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

BIOL 351.title: Plant Physiology I
BIOL 351.description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. Restricted to Majors and Honours students in Biology.
BIOL 351.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL 121 and one of CHEM 123, CHEM 130; or (b) SCIE 001

BIOL 352.title: Plant Physiology II: Plant Development
BIOL 352.description: Introduction to the processes involved in growth and development: cell division, tissue culture, meristems, differentiation, and the action of major growth regulators, and photomorphogenesis. Emphasis on experimental approaches.
BIOL 352.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234; or (b) FRST 302

BIOL 361.title: Neural and Muscular Physiology
BIOL 361.description: Excitable membranes, neural signaling and transmission; transduction and coding of sensory information; muscle contraction.

BIOL 362.title: Cellular Dynamics
BIOL 362.description: The cytoskeleton, cell dynamics, and regulation of cellular activities. Preference will be given to Majors or Honours students in Biology and Combined Honours Biophysics.
BIOL 362.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of APBI 312, APBI 351, BIOL 260, BIOL 351, BIOL 352, BIOL 361, FRST 311

BIOL 364.title: Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology
BIOL 364.description: Cardiovascular, respiratory, and osmoregulatory physiology. Preference will be given to students who are in Biology, Nutritional Sciences, and Combined Honours Biophysics.
BIOL 364.prerequisiteText: BIOL 204 and one of BIOL 260, BIOL 361

BIOL 370.title: Principles of Muscle Physiology and Energetics
BIOL 370.description: Introduction to the structure and function of the muscular system, metabolism and energetics from a comparative perspective across vertebrates and invertebrates.
BIOL 370.prerequisiteText: BIOL 260 and one of BIOL 200, BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203

BIOL 371.title: Principles of Neurobiology I
BIOL 371.description: Introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system, excitable membranes, and synaptic signaling using representative vertebrate and invertebrate species. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 371.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 260, NSCI 200, PSYC 270, PSYC 271, PSYC 304, CAPS 301

BIOL 372.title: Principles of Neurobiology II
BIOL 372.description: Examination of the neural systems underlying sensation, action, and complex behaviours using representative vertebrate and invertebrate species. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

BIOL 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
BIOL 398.description: Work experience in an industrial setting, taken during Winter Session (Term 2) of third-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology.

BIOL 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
BIOL 399.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following third-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology.

BIOL 401.title: Theory of Evolutionary Dynamics
BIOL 401.description: Evolution as a dynamical system based on ecological interactions. Adaptive dynamics and evolutionary game theory. .
BIOL 401.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 301 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

BIOL 402.title: Aquatic Ecology
BIOL 402.description: Theoretical and applied limnology; ecology of inland water organisms in relation to physical, chemical and biological factors. One weekend field trip required.
BIOL 402.prerequisiteText: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200

BIOL 403.title: Microbial Ecology
BIOL 403.description: Theoretical and applied ecology of microbes. Focus on microbial symbionts of animals, plants and seaweeds. Research project development through critical analysis of microbial ecological literature and computational analysis of ecological data.
BIOL 403.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 121, SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 230 and one of BIOL_V 300, FRST_V 231, STAT_V 200. 4th-year class standing

BIOL 404.title: Ecological Methodology
BIOL 404.description: Design, execution, and analysis of ecological surveys and experiments. Practical field methods for estimating population metrics and describing community structure. Computer techniques for the statistical analysis of ecological data.
BIOL 404.prerequisiteText: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200

BIOL 406.title: Plant Ecology I
BIOL 406.description: Plant community ecology including a consideration of the major approaches to sampling, analyzing and interpreting vegetation patterns. Instruction given in field work and computer analysis of field data.

BIOL 408.title: Principles of Applied Ecology
BIOL 408.description: Principles of animal and community ecology applicable to the management of animal resources; application of statistical and computer techniques for measuring, analyzing, modelling, and simulating resource systems; problems of multiple resource use.

BIOL 409.title: Field Course in Ecology
BIOL 409.description: A two-week intensive course in field methods used in ecology. Fieldwork for this course is normally in the summer. A fee will be assessed for living and traveling expenses. Pre-registration required.
BIOL 409.prerequisiteText: BIOL 230 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200

BIOL 410.title: Current Topics in Animal Behaviour
BIOL 410.description: Lectures and seminar discussions on selected topics in animal behaviour.

BIOL 411.title: Insect Ecology
BIOL 411.description: Behavioural, population and community ecology of insects. Interactions between insects and plants and the application of the principles of insect ecology to biological control of insects and weeds.

BIOL 412.title: Plant Biogeography
BIOL 412.description: Description and interpretation of present and past floristic vegetational patterns; integration of evolutionary, ecological, and plant biogeographical concepts. Terrestrial and aquatic plants are considered. Restricted to students of third and fourth years.

BIOL 413.title: Zoogeography
BIOL 413.description: The role of physical, ecological, and evolutionary processes in determining the geographic distribution of animals including humans, with implications for speciation and conservation. Restricted to students in third and fourth year.

BIOL 415.title: Evolutionary Processes in Plants
BIOL 415.description: Experimental and comparative analysis of evolutionary processes, speciation, and phylogenetic patterns in plants.

BIOL 416.title: Principles of Conservation Biology
BIOL 416.description: Ecological basis of conserving biological diversity and ecosystem services; application of ecological theory to global and local conservation problems in the context of economic, legal, political, and social perspectives. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

BIOL 417.title: Phylogenetic Biology
BIOL 417.description: Biodiversity from an evolutionary perspective. The evolutionary (phylogenetic) tree of genetic descent that links all organisms: its reconstruction, interpretation, and implications for fields from ecology to molecular biology.
BIOL 417.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234

BIOL 418.title: Evolutionary Ecology
BIOL 418.description: Ecological adaptation and evolutionary processes in contemporary populations; natural selection, variation, optimization, foraging theory, coevolution, arms races; life history theory, evolution of sex, sexual selection, evolution in managed populations.

BIOL 420.title: Ocean Conservation and Sustainability
BIOL 420.description: An interdisciplinary conservation course with a solutions-oriented approach to marine issues, drawing from natural sciences, social sciences, business, law, and communication. .

BIOL 421.title: Plant-Microbe Interactions
BIOL 421.description: Biology and physiology of selected plant-microbe relationships. Impacts of plant-microbe relationships on society.
BIOL 421.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of BIOC 202, BIOC 203, BIOL 201, BIOL 233, BIOL 234, BIOL 260

BIOL 423.title: Plant Stress Ecophysiology
BIOL 423.description: Molecular mechanisms of plant responses to extreme environments. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

BIOL 424.title: Tropical Ecology and Conservation
BIOL 424.description: Ecology, function, history and conservation of tropical systems. Focus on ecological and evolutionary principles using tropical landscapes as a geographic template. Assessment of factors that make tropical systems vulnerable to degradation. Research project development using analysis of tropical ecology literature.
BIOL 424.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 121 or SCIE_V 001 and one of BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, GEOS_V 207, GEOB_V 207

BIOL 425.title: Biomechanics
BIOL 425.description: An analytical approach to the study of skeletal mechanics and animal locomotion. Selected topics in the structure and properties of biological materials, the functional design of skeletons for locomotion, and the fluid mechanics of swimming and flight.

BIOL 426.title: Mammalogy
BIOL 426.description: Natural history, behavioral ecology and conservation of terrestrial mammals. The laboratory includes classification, life histories, and ecology, with particular attention to species from British Columbia.

BIOL 427.title: Ornithology and Herpetology
BIOL 427.description: Ecology, evolution, behavior, and conservation of birds, amphibians, and reptiles. Laboratories and field projects will focus on identification, systematics, and natural history, with particular attention to species from British Columbia.

BIOL 428.title: Evolutionary Morphology of Marine Invertebrates
BIOL 428.description: Comparative analysis of marine invertebrate morphology from a macroevolutionary perspective. Origin and evolution of reoccurring adaptations in meiofaunal, benthic, pelagic, and deep-sea invertebrates, including their larval stages.
BIOL 428.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 205 and 3rd-year class standing or higher

BIOL 430.title: Genome Evolution
BIOL 430.description: Integration of molecular genetics and genomics with evolutionary biology. Emphasis on the evolutionary dynamics of genomes and the evolutionary implications of recent discoveries in molecular genetics and genomics.
BIOL 430.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 335, BIOL_V 336, BIOL_V 338, BIOT_V 380

BIOL 431.title: Evolutionary Cell Biology
BIOL 431.description: Ultrastructure, biogenesis, and evolution of eukaryotic cells and cell organelles, including their macromolecular basis.

BIOL 432.title: Research Strategies and Techniques in Cell Biology
BIOL 432.description: Major physiological mechanisms that define eukaryotic cells, explored through student visits to UBC research laboratories and discussion of recent scientific literature, with emphasis on the techniques and strategies that enable researchers to test hypotheses and advance new concepts.
BIOL 432.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 200 and one of BIOL_V 233, BIOL_V 234 and 4th-year class standing

BIOL 433.title: Plant Genetics
BIOL 433.description: Emphasis on molecular aspects. Systems and techniques for genetic analysis in plants; isolation and regulation of plant genes; genetic dissection of plant-specific processes; transposable elements; gene transfer in plants; cytoplasmic inheritance; genetic engineering. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

BIOL 434.title: Population Genetics
BIOL 434.description: Theoretical and experimental aspects of population and quantitative genetics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
BIOL 434.prerequisiteText: BIOL 336 and either (a) BIOL 200 and one of BIOL 233, BIOL 234; or (b) FRST 302

BIOL 436.title: Integrated Functional Genomics
BIOL 436.description: Global transcript, protein, and metabolite profiling technologies and their integration; applications focus on plant functions and plant interactions with pathogens and pests. One of BIOL_V 335, BIOL_V 338, BIOT_V 380.

BIOL 437.title: Laboratory in Animal Cell Molecular Biology
BIOL 437.description: The use of recombinant DNA techniques to explore problems in animal developmental biology.
BIOL 437.prerequisiteText: All of BIOL 331, BIOL 335 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203

BIOL 438.title: Zoological Physics
BIOL 438.description: Animal systems viewed from a physicist's perspective. Topics include sensory systems, energy budgets, locomotion, internal flows, physical advantages of grouping.
BIOL 438.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001

BIOL 439.title: Advanced Microscopy Techniques
BIOL 439.description: Microscopy techniques used in biological research. Principles, applications and hands-on training of optical and electron microscopy. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: .
BIOL 439.corequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 448, BIOL_V 449 and Fourth-year standing

BIOL 440.title: Plant Genomics
BIOL 440.description: Concepts, principles, applications, and recent discoveries in genome structure, genetics, and comparative genomics in plants with a focus on economically important plants.

BIOL 441.title: Advanced Topics in Cell Biology
BIOL 441.description: Analysis of cellular organelles and the intracellular traffic between them, concentrating on mammalian cell systems.
BIOL 441.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 340, BIOL 341 and one of BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 370, BIOL 371

BIOL 445.title: Darwin's Fishes
BIOL 445.description: A series of computer-assisted lectures using ichthyology and the work of Charles Darwin to illustrate basic principles of biology, and their practical implementation, i.e., how biologists select research programs, generate and test hypotheses, and present their case to peers and the public.

prerequisite.raw: 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science is required

BIOL 445.prerequisiteText: 3rd-year class standing or higher in Science is required

BIOL 446.title: History and Philosophy of Biology
BIOL 446.description: The nature of science, this history of evolutionary and molecular biology, philosophical questions about scientific methods and fundamental conclusions of biology.

prerequisite.raw: 4th-year class standing in any degree program

BIOL 446.prerequisiteText: 4th-year class standing in any degree program

BIOL 447.title: Principles and Methodology in Biological Research
BIOL 447.description: Seminars, debates, workshops and tutorials designed to produce competence in specific areas of Biology. Restricted to Honours students in Biology.

BIOL 448.title: Directed Studies in Biology
BIOL 448.description: A course designed to allow students to undertake an investigation on a specific topic as agreed upon by the faculty member and the student. Permission of the supervisor required. No more than six credits of BIOL_V 448 may be taken with the same supervisor.

BIOL 449.title: Directed Biological Research
BIOL 449.description: A course designed to allow students to undertake a research project in selected fields. Open only to Honours students in Biology, with permission of the supervisor. Presentation of a thesis and an oral examination are required.

BIOL 450.title: Molecular Adaptation of Animals to the Environment
BIOL 450.description: Physiological, biochemical, and molecular strategies of adaptation of animals to environmental challenges. The evolution of genetic and biochemical systems, and their impact on animal structure and function.
BIOL 450.prerequisiteText: One of APBI 311, BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 364, BIOL 370, BIOL 371 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203

BIOL 451.title: Comparative Neurobiology
BIOL 451.description: Advanced investigations of the evolution of animal nervous systems, integrating studies of diverse species to understand fundamental neurobiology.
BIOL 451.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 371, BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370

BIOL 453.title: Insect Physiology
BIOL 453.description: Physiological adaptations used by insects, including adaptations used to survive in extreme environments. Homeostatic mechanisms, neurophysiology, and experimental techniques.
BIOL 453.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 204, BIOL_V 205, BIOL_V 327, APBI_V 327 and one of BIOL_V 361, BIOL_V 364, BIOL_V 370, BIOL_V 371, APBI_V 311

BIOL 454.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
BIOL 454.description: Selected topics in physiology emphasizing comparisons between diverse phylogenetic groups of animals.

BIOL 455.title: Comparative Neurobiology
BIOL 455.description: Current approaches in neurobiology, from the cellular to the behavioural level, are examined using representatives of vertebrate and invertebrate nervous systems.
BIOL 455.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 361, BIOL 362, BIOL 364, CAPS 301, PSYC 360

BIOL 456.title: Comparative and Molecular Endocrinology
BIOL 456.description: A comparative study of vertebrate and invertebrate endocrinology.

BIOL 457.title: Comparative Environmental Physiology
BIOL 457.description: A survey of physiological adaptions of animals to different environments.

BIOL 458.title: Developmental Neurobiology
BIOL 458.description: Cellular, molecular and physiological aspects of nervous system development with applications to understanding adult nervous system function and neurological disorders.

BIOL 459.title: Neurobiology of Sensory and Motor Systems
BIOL 459.description: Analysis of the mechanisms of sensory processing and motor orchestration using vertebrate and invertebrate model systems. Neural circuit structure, specialization, information coding, integration, and behaviour.
BIOL 459.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370

BIOL 460.title: Neurobiology of Vision
BIOL 460.description: Advanced investigation of animal vision; critical analysis of recent literature and research project development in visual neurobiology.
BIOL 460.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 372, CAPS 301, PSYC 304, PSYC 367, PSYC 370

BIOL 462.title: Ecological Plant Biochemistry
BIOL 462.description: The structure, biosynthesis, distribution and biological function of secondary plant metabolites.
BIOL 462.prerequisiteText: Either a) BIOL_V 200 and one of either BIOL_V 201 or BIOC_V 202, or b) BIOT_V 380

BIOL 463.title: Gene Regulation in Development
BIOL 463.description: Control of gene expression in development; the genetic and physiological basis of epigenetic determination; inductive interactions.
BIOL 463.prerequisiteText: Either (a) BIOL 335 and one of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203; or (b) BIOT 380

BIOL 464.title: Animal Developmental Genetics
BIOL 464.description: Role of genes in embryonic development. Emphasis on tissue specific expression patterns and the role of genetic networks in establishing cell types.

BIOL 465.title: Diversity and Evolution of Fishes
BIOL 465.description: Introduction to fish diversity, with a focus on their phylogenetic interrelationships and the evolutionary, ecological, and biogeographic processes involved in generating patterns of fish biodiversity.

BIOL 466.title: Applied Biology of Fishes
BIOL 466.description: Physiological ecology and exploitation biology of teleost fishes; computer-based analysis and modeling of fish populations.

BIOL 488.title: Topics in Biology
BIOL 488.description: Selected topics in a specific area within Biology. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the Department.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a Life Science specialization

BIOL 488.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a Life Science specialization

BIOL 490.title: Student Directed Seminars
BIOL 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Normally not suitable as a specific BIOL program elective.

BIOL 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
BIOL 498.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology.

BIOL 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
BIOL 499.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Winter Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth-year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Biology.

BIOL 501.title: Quantitative Methods in Ecology and Evolution
BIOL 501.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 300 or equivalent and graduate student standing

BIOL 503.title: Microbial Ecology
BIOL 503.description: Theoretical and applied ecology of microbes. Focus on microbial symbionts of animals, plants and seaweeds. Critical analysis of microbial ecological literature and computational analysis of ecological data. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: .

BIOL 509.title: Population and Quantitative Genetics
BIOL 509.description: Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

BIOL 533.title: Plant Genetics
BIOL 533.description: Emphasis on molecular aspects. Systems and techniques for genetic analysis in plants; isolation and regulation of plant genes; genetic dissection of plant-specific processes; transposable elements; gene transfer in plants; cytoplasmic inheritance; genetic engineering. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: .

BIOL 535.title: Teaching and Learning in the Life Sciences

BIOL 537.title: Topics in Biotechnology
BIOL 537.description: Research reviews, class discussions, and presentations about current research in the diverse areas of biotechnology. Topics include the research interests of members of the UBC Biotechnology Laboratory. .

BIOL 539.title: Advanced Microscopy Techniques
BIOL 539.description: Microscopy techniques used in biological research. Principles, applications and hands-on training of optical and electron microscopy. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists: .
